themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Hazards Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street signs and outside-building structural issues surged THIS WEEK, with 5 dangling sign complaints (vs. 1.4 weekly average) and 3 outside-building complaints (vs. 0.4 weekly average), suggesting rapid deterioration of public infrastructure safety.
evidence: Street Sign - Dangling complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (264% spike, z-score: 4.23)
Outside Building complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Both spikes emerged simultaneously, suggesting common cause (weather, deferred maintenance, or contractor activity)
reporting_angles: Walk Greenpoint/Williamsburg streets to identify and photograph specific hazards; interview NYCDOT about inspection schedules
Cross-reference DOB permits (1,300 filed in 90 days, 32 demolitions) with spike timing—are active construction sites causing structural damage?

themes_detail.label: Street Vending Enforcement Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints exploded THIS WEEK to 10 complaints (vs. 1.1 weekly average, +789%) while mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 8 (vs. 0.6 average, +1180%), suggesting either major regulatory crackdown, new vendor influx, or community backlash against street commerce.
evidence: Vendor Enforcement complaints: 10 THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (789% spike, z-score: 4.52)
Mobile Food Vendor complaints: 8 LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (1180% spike, z-score: 7.43—highest z-score in dataset)
Dual spike suggests coordinated enforcement action or rapid market change in informal economy
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD, DOH, and Parks Enforcement to understand what triggered sudden enforcement surge this week
Interview street vendors in Williamsburg and Greenpoint about enforcement pressure, permit costs, and whether they're being forced out
Investigate whether new vendor permits or licenses issued recently drove influx and subsequent complaints from residents

themes_detail.label: Indoor Sewage System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Indoor sewage complaints spiked 700% 2 weeks ago (3 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average), and although not this week's peak, this represents a critical infrastructure failure pattern that persists in the district.
evidence: Indoor Sewage complaints: 3 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Heat/hot water also remains top category (2,321 complaints over 90 days), suggesting aging building infrastructure
DEP has standing budget request for 'Other capital budget request' (repeated annually, unsolved)
reporting_angles: Request DEP data on sewer main breaks and cleanings in Greenpoint/Williamsburg in past month—are three complaints tied to single infrastructure failure?
Interview affected residents about timeline, whether issue is ongoing; check if complaints are from same buildings or scattered
Connect to historic Greenpoint sewage issues and oil spill legacy (context for aging infrastructure vulnerability)

themes_detail.label: Parking Pressure Intensifies
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints jumped 34% two weeks ago (444 complaints vs. 332.5 weekly average) and remain the highest-volume complaint category (4,399 over 90 days), with sustained pressure in a district long plagued by development-driven parking shortages.
evidence: Illegal Parking: 444 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 332.5 weekly average (34% spike, z-score: 3.63)
Illegal Parking is #1 complaint type overall (4,399 in 90 days), outpacing heat/hot water 2:1
DOT has standing budget request to 'Improve traffic and pedestrian safety, including traffic calming' (repeated annually, unresolved)
reporting_angles: Map parking complaint hotspots against active ULURP rezonings (200 Kent Ave, 20 Berry St, 289 Kent Ave, Monitor Point) to show development-driven parking squeeze
Interview residents about whether recent construction projects removed parking spaces or created new demand
Quantify: how many parking spots have been lost in past 2 years vs. how many new units added?

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Decline
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints dropped 28% THIS WEEK (103 vs. 142.2 weekly average), a statistically significant anomaly that breaks the expected seasonal pattern and warrants investigation into whether enforcement or behavioral changes are real.
evidence: Noise - Residential: 103 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 142.2 weekly average (28% DROP, z-score: -4.27)
This is the only major category with a statistically significant downward spike, suggesting real behavior change
Noise remains #3 complaint category overall (1,854 over 90 days), but this week's dip is anomalous
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD enforcement to confirm whether noise enforcement increased this week
Investigate seasonal factors: did weather change (warmer temps = outdoor activity shift)?
Check if nightlife venues closed or altered hours; interview community board about any enforcement campaigns
